# Define tutorial packaging format and validation tooling

## Description

Defines the tutorial packaging format — the standard that makes a tutorial a
versioned, testable artifact independent of Dashboard releases — together with
the validation tooling that mechanically checks a tutorial package against it.
The format specifies tutorial metadata, pinned images, and a validation
manifest, and conveys enough information for a consumer to launch a tutorial
(notebook-based vs pipeline-based, which image to use) without any per-tutorial
knowledge baked into the Dashboard.

This is a spec epic: it defines the standard only. The real curated tutorials
are authored and packaged elsewhere in this strategy as users of the format.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial package format: metadata describing the tutorial
  (identity, kind — notebook-based or pipeline-based, core journey covered),
  pinned images for reproducible execution, and a validation manifest
  describing how the tutorial is tested.
- Define versioning rules so tutorial packages can be released, updated, and
  tested independently of Dashboard releases.
- Provide validation tooling that mechanically checks a package against the
  format: conforming packages pass; malformed packages fail with actionable
  errors.
- Validate the format with minimal stub fixtures: one synthetic notebook-type
  package and one synthetic pipeline-type package that pass validation. These
  stubs are validation scaffolding proving the format checks mechanically —
  they are not usable tutorials and are not part of the curated tutorial set.
- Document the format so that other teams can package tutorials against it
  (the contribution documentation will reference it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A tutorial packaging format is defined covering metadata, pinned images, and
  a validation manifest, with explicit versioning (HLR-3).
- A conformant package of each kind — notebook-based and pipeline-based —
  passes validation; a malformed package fails with an actionable error
  message.
- Stub fixtures exist for both kinds and pass validation; they are explicitly
  labeled synthetic validation scaffolding, not deliverable tutorials
  (spec-vs-content boundary).
- The format distinguishes notebook-based from pipeline-based tutorials, so a
  consumer can determine launch behavior from package metadata alone.
- A team outside the format's authors can package a working tutorial using the
  format documentation alone.
- Tutorials packaged per the format are testable without a Dashboard release
  (validation runs against the package, not the gallery).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (primary): tutorial packaging format for versioned, independently
  testable tutorials.
- Enables HLR-1 and HLR-2: the format is the contract the gallery consumes and
  the tutorials are packaged against.

# Tutorial gallery and one-click launch in the Dashboard

## Description

Delivers the user-facing tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated gallery
surface from which a user launches a tutorial into their own project with one
click — opening a workbench with the tutorial notebook loaded, or importing the
tutorial pipeline into the project. The gallery reads tutorial packages that
conform to the tutorial packaging format and holds no per-tutorial logic, so
tutorials can be versioned and updated independently of Dashboard releases.

## Scope

- A gallery surface in the Dashboard listing the available curated tutorial
  packages (curated set only this release — no community or partner
  submission tooling).
- One-click launch of a notebook-based tutorial: opens a workbench in the
  user's project with the tutorial notebook loaded, using the pinned image
  from the package metadata.
- One-click launch of a pipeline-based tutorial: imports the pipeline into
  the user's project's Data Science Pipelines instance.
- Launch mechanics driven by package metadata per the tutorial packaging
  format (kind, pinned images) — no hardcoded per-tutorial handling in
  Dashboard code.
- Implementation through the Dashboard's existing interfaces: workbench
  creation via Notebook CRs and pipeline import via the pipelines REST API,
  per the platform architecture (the Dashboard reads and writes CRs and owns
  no data plane).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial
  into their own project with one click (HLR-1).
- Launching a notebook-based tutorial opens a workbench in the user's project
  with the tutorial notebook loaded.
- Launching a pipeline-based tutorial imports the pipeline into the user's
  project.
- The gallery lists and one-click-launches every tutorial package conforming
  to the packaging format, verified against conformant packages of both kinds
  — including the packaging format's validation fixtures, which cover one
  notebook-type and one pipeline-type package — and, as they become available,
  the curated tutorials.
- No per-tutorial hardcoding: adding a conformant tutorial package to the
  curated set requires no Dashboard code change (tutorials version
  independently of Dashboard releases).
- Existing Dashboard build and test pipelines remain green with the gallery
  changes merged.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (primary): tutorial gallery with one-click launch into the user's
  project.

Authors the notebook-based tutorials of the curated getting-started set — the
maintained, tested content that users launch from the tutorial gallery. This
epic covers the core journeys delivered as notebooks: first workbench, data
prep, first training run, first deployment, and first RAG app. Each tutorial is
an authored, curated notebook packaged per the tutorial packaging format and
tested against the current release.

This is content-authoring work (sample notebooks), distinct from the Dashboard
product code: it produces the tutorials themselves, not gallery or launch
mechanics.

## Scope

- Author five notebook-based tutorials covering the core journeys: first
  workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, first RAG app.
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format: metadata, pinned
  workbench image, and validation manifest (notebook-based kind).
- Curate the set for coherence: a consistent style and difficulty ramp so a
  new user progresses naturally from first workbench to first RAG app.
- Test each tutorial against the current release: it runs successfully on a
  workbench in a user project with the pinned image — exercising the workbench
  path (notebook server, pinned image) and passively validating the Notebooks
  component, which requires no code changes for this strategy.

  notebook-based portion of HLR-2).
- Each tutorial passes the tutorial packaging format's validation (packaged as
  the notebook-based kind, with pinned image and validation manifest).
- Each tutorial is tested against the current release: launched on a workbench
  in a project, it runs to completion with the pinned image.
- Pinned images recorded in the package metadata make tutorial runs
  reproducible.
- Each tutorial is launchable into a user's project per the packaging format's
  launch contract (notebook-based kind: opens a workbench with the notebook
  loaded).

  journeys, tested against the current release — this epic delivers the five
